runtime_notes: Claude Code agent-team wording is adapted by SKILL.md into Codex inline role-prompt usage.
The Codex-only codex/ adapter profile is optional and disabled by default; it provides planner metadata, agent-team templates, hook metadata, and quality gates for explicit full-runtime use.
The maintainer's local ARS checkout was not used as a write target.
Upstream slash commands are vendored as prompt recipes and emulated through the Codex SKILL.md alias router; Codex does not register native slash commands.
Vendored upstream workflow entry files are renamed from SKILL.md to WORKFLOW.md in this Codex package so Codex registers only the root academic-research-suite router skill.
Vague paper-topic requests without a clear research question are routed to deep-research socratic mode before outline, drafting, or full pipeline execution.
docs/superpowers/ is intentionally excluded; it contains upstream Claude Code development plans referencing superpowers:* sub-skills which do not exist in the Codex runtime.
User-facing setup docs include reinstall, /skills verification, and Codex CLI smoke-test guidance for existing-session cache behavior.
Root README.md and SKILL.md define Codex install/runtime behavior; vendored upstream docs remain traceability/reference material unless explicitly adapted here.
The v3.7.1 pattern-protection validator is patched to resolve git object paths from the nested Codex vendored root.

The spec-consistency validator is patched for the Codex distribution: non-vendored .claude/CLAUDE.md is skipped, excluded showcase PDF links are not treated as broken, and WORKFLOW.md replaces internal SKILL.md entry files.
The shared metadata linter auto-detects this Codex distribution and validates vendored WORKFLOW.md entry files instead of upstream SKILL.md files.
The Codex package carries scripts/codex_v3_6_7_block_baseline.json so first-time vendored trees can enforce v3.6.7 block byte-equivalence before Git history contains the upstream manifest.
The Codex audit wrapper is patched to run on macOS stock Bash 3.2+ instead of requiring Bash 4+.
Vendored test utilities keep macOS stock Python 3.9 compatibility where Codex local validation depends on it.

ARS v3.21.0 release content (peeled commit 2b639c12ee4e7c694a32336cc59dc2616e0d89fe, 2026-08-18) is the tracked upstream content; component versions are deep-research 2.12.1, academic-paper 3.3.1, academic-paper-reviewer 1.11.1, and academic-pipeline/suite 3.21.0. Nested upstream .github workflows, release-discipline tools, and root agents mirrors are preserved for traceability and upstream self-tests but are not repo-level CI or Codex entrypoints. Claude/plugin loader files under .claude, .claude-plugin, upstream skills aliases, and runtime log files remain intentionally excluded.
ARS_MODEL_TIERING is classification-compatible but remains advisory in Codex unless the runtime exposes explicit per-dispatch model selection; unset and unsupported cases keep the active model.
The upstream model-tiering validator excludes the separately vendored experiment-agent tree from its frozen 39-agent ARS classification sweep.
Korean intent triggers are propagated into the root Codex router and optional full-runtime planner because vendored WORKFLOW.md frontmatter is not independently registered.
The live cross-model smoke test remains manual-only and cross-model verification retains the explicit provider, content, credential, and consent gate.

The v3.17 canonical cross-model handoff envelope is preserved; dispatched owners emit a transport request and the dispatching Codex context validates and routes it without widening owner capabilities.
The v3.17 tools allowlist remains a least-privilege role boundary; Codex inline execution does not reinterpret Claude tool names as additional authority.

The degradation registry, executable panel checker, pipeline-boundary lock, tools-allowlist lock, and hermetic transport fixtures are vendored with their upstream tests; the pipeline-orchestrator content-lock hash is updated only for the Codex WORKFLOW.md path overlay.

The v3.18 fixed-seat cross-model Reviewer 2 track and re-review judge pass remain gated by explicit provider configuration and content consent; dispatch failure or single-family execution is disclosed rather than simulated.

The v3.18 citation-cache staleness advisory, opt-in live re-validation, risk-stratified claim gate, scope and novelty advisories, and held-out pipeline-behavior set are preserved with their upstream tests and schemas.

The upstream SessionStart update reminder is vendored for traceability and testing but is not installed or executed by Codex; plugin users update by refreshing the ars-codex marketplace and re-adding the plugin, while direct skill users reinstall manually.
The v3.19 local-PDF read-integrity preflight is preserved with its pypdf-backed sidecar contract; FAIL and UNAVAILABLE remain distinct, and missing verification is never promoted to PASS.

The v3.20.1 human-read ledger requires a user-owned read_scope on every new mark; explicit unknown and legacy records with absent scope resolve to coverage_unknown, partial coverage stays visible, locators are accepted only for sections scope, and the deterministic resolver fails visibly on invalid ledger state.
The v3.19 claim-strength ladder, revision-evidence bundle, deterministic token-conservation checker, and held-out revision-claim-drift set are preserved as advisory-first revision guards.

ARS-Codex Desktop plugin packaging uses a materialized skills directory under plugins/ars-codex/skills instead of a symlink so Windows plugin caches can register the bundled academic-research-suite skill.
Cross-model API behavior is disabled by default and requires explicit user request, provider configuration, and user consent before any external upload.

The community-maintained Pi wrapper (pi/ plus the root package.json pi-package manifest) is vendored for traceability only; it targets the Pi harness and upstream SKILL.md paths, so it is not a Codex entrypoint and is not loadable from this renamed WORKFLOW.md tree.

The #574/#611/#615 reviewer-contract lint family (check_decision_contract, check_reviewer_finding_contract, check_reviewer_role_label, venue_disclosure_contract_harness, and their tests) is path-adapted to the Codex WORKFLOW.md overlay, matching the existing pipeline-boundary content-lock adaptation.

The v3.19+ reviewer hardening track (role-scoped scoring contract, typed evidence anchors, three-gate Stage 3' re-review contract, dispatch harness, arithmetic-receipt grammar, empty-dissent rule) and its held-out eval sets are preserved with their upstream tests; eval cohorts are measurement records, not Codex runtime instructions.

The v3.20 contained Codex citation transport is an explicit ARS_CROSS_MODEL_TRANSPORT=codex selector only for one-reference Stage 2.5/4.5 checks. It requires Codex CLI 0.147.0 or newer, ARS_CROSS_MODEL, the exact Logged in using ChatGPT attestation, and explicit provider/content/cost consent; it accepts no caller-authored prompt or path, does not cover reviewer/DA/calibration/re-review/checkpoint/handoff calls, and has no automatic API fallback.

The Codex citation transport uses an EOF-complete post-terminal drain: turn/completed is provisional until stdin is closed, the parent exits cleanly, and stdout/stderr reach EOF within the bounded drain. Late forbidden or malformed events, timeout, nonzero exit, reader failure, or stderr overflow fail visibly rather than being discarded.

The v3.20 PDF content classifier is an opt-in --classify-content extension whose optional dependency is separately pinned in requirements-pdf-content-classifier.txt. It runs in a process-isolated worker and emits only TEXT_AVAILABLE/OCR_RECOMMENDED/unavailable advisory data while the structural PASS/FAIL/UNAVAILABLE decision and STRUCTURE_ONLY verdict scope remain authoritative; dependency absence is deterministic and no automatic OCR or anchor gate is wired.

The v3.20 shared Phase E evidence rows are deterministic, source-bound checkpoint artifacts that replay against explicit session-held bytes. They preserve the existing citation verdict/gate and never infer human-read state; rendering, consistency, or content-coverage advisories do not become integrity verdicts or clean-document certificates.

The v3.20 non-ranking revision roadmap is proposal-only until exact author choices are recorded in the separate author-adjudication sidecar. Author decisions and correction authority are never inferred or fabricated, and optional cross-run adjudication-activity capture is local, best-effort, nonblocking, and excluded from model prompts and handoffs.

The v3.20 review-target contract binds author-confirmed discipline/venue/track/contribution context and resolved criterion pointers across formative, internal, and external review. Missing context is not inferred; criteria-binding conformance cannot alter integrity verdicts, checkpoints, editorial arithmetic, or author triage, and new-data or intent-changing remedies remain author choices.

The v3.20 human-subjects contracts keep review-ethics and data-protection authority axes separate, preserve exact authority pointers, and block profile-dependent results when scope, source currency, or applicability is unresolved. Outputs remain institution-owned navigation aids and never fabricate an IRB/REC determination, legal advice, authorization, readiness, or institutional timeline.

The v3.20 bibliographic-integrity carrier preserves resolver/list observations, heuristic indicators, retraction disagreement/staleness, provenance, and degradation without minting a clean result or replacing citation-finalizer policy authority. The preregistration cross-document carrier is replay-bound, nonblocking, LLM-ADVISORY/UNMEASURED, and never a score, rewrite, protocol duplicate, consent record, agreement finding, or clean-document certificate.

The v3.20 #675 offline/no-call envelope resolves its suite_commit from this package manifest when the nested vendored ARS tree intentionally has no .git directory. The manifest source lock substitutes only for local HEAD discovery; frozen asset hashes remain the byte-level authority and no subprocess, model, network, or live probe is introduced.

The v3.20.1 Socratic non-generation contract treats non-convergence, elapsed rounds, and stagnation as insufficient consent for system-authored candidate research questions; generation requires an explicit user request and a visible exit from the default mode.

The v3.20.1 reviewer contract retires live numeric scores, weights, aggregates, and score trajectories in favor of evidence-anchored categorical criterion judgements. Seat and current Schema 6 outputs remain NOT_CALIBRATED, and six-axis panel provenance never becomes a binary independence claim.

The v3.20.1 claim registry reports exact-span and raw-byte coverage over registered E1 claims without claiming semantic extraction completeness or manuscript correctness. Claim-strength drift dispositions remain a separate evidence sidecar and do not mint revision authority.

The v3.20.1 claim-standing stance runner/renderer and blind within-session ideation assignment gate are bounded evaluation infrastructure. Their receipts preserve consent, no-call, provenance, and unmeasured boundaries rather than certifying correctness or diversity.

The v3.21 data-flow map, control-availability matrix, stage-capability matrix, risk register, governance statement, and audit record are preserved as transparency and traceability surfaces; their evidence labels and residual gaps are not promoted into effectiveness or certification claims.

The v3.21 claim-standing pipeline wiring remains a user-requested advisory after an eligible Stage 2.5/4.5 Claim Registry row. Eligibility never dispatches work, affirmative plan-bound consent is mandatory, and absent, cancelled, invalidated, or stale consent produces no external call.

Codex bibliographic network routing is defined by the root SKILL.md: ordinary discovery and inline ingest use Codex browsing, the four Python resolver clients require an explicit programmatic-verification request, and invoking ars-full alone does not launch them. This is an intentional adapter boundary, not an upstream runtime claim.

The separately vendored experiment-agent tree tracks its upstream v1.1.0 (session resume for study_manager_agent, study-state protocol and templates); its .claude/ and .github/ upstream dev files remain excluded and its entry file keeps the WORKFLOW.md rename with the Codex data_access_level/task_type frontmatter overlay.
